verdict.rationale: Google Cloud's own documentation describes Workload Identity Federation, which gives on-premises and multicloud workloads access through federated identities instead of a service account key. That directly addresses the no-long-lived-key goal. The pack, however, holds only that single sentence, with no detail on short-lived token issuance, CI/OIDC setup, or an end-to-end walkthrough. missing for 10: evidence of short-lived token lifetimes, explicit CI provider (e.g. OIDC from CI systems) integration docs, end-to-end setup documentation, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a security engineer, nothing ships a long-lived key — OIDC/workload identity federation issues short-lived credentials to CI and services, documented end to end

citations.quote: Using Workload Identity Federation, you can provide on-premises or multicloud workloads with access to Google Cloud resources by using federated identities instead of a service account key.
